public_rationale: In June 2024, Scott said next-generation models 'could pass PhD qualifying exams', compared with GPT-4 matching high schoolers on AP exams. He added that this 'probably sounds like a bigger deal than it actually is'. He did not name GPT-5 in the coverage I read. 'Blow away PhDs' is Marcus's paraphrase. Whether GPT-5's gains were 'far more modest' has no stated measure. OpenAI reports GPT-5 pro scored 88.4% on GPQA, a graduate-level science test, which points to large benchmark gains. Critics instead point to real-world limits. Because the claim turns on a subjective comparison against a hedged hint, I cannot score it fairly as true or false.
limitations: I did not find a full transcript of Scott's talk.
